title: Convert Release to an RLinf-tracking adaptation repository
goal: Rework Release from a trimmed framework snapshot into a traceable RLinf-based Franka/Pico adaptation repository with explicit upstream governance, maintained adaptation boundaries, repeatable compatibility checks, and unchanged hardware safety constraints.
doneWhen: Release history is based on the approved RLinf upstream commit and has an upstream remote configured for RLinf/RLinf.
Release-owned Franka/Pico adaptations, configuration, tools, documentation, and focused checks have clear paths and ownership.

The repository documents origin versus upstream responsibilities, supported scope versus merely present upstream code, approved baseline provenance, and a repeatable upstream synchronization procedure.
Compatibility checks cover Release layout, launch/config linkage, imports, locks, and no-hardware validation; hardware limitations are explicitly stated.
No change weakens existing control or hardware safety rules.
decisions: The prior trimmed-framework Release design is superseded by the user's Release business-logic change dated 2026-10-19.
RLinf is the upstream framework subject; Release is the project's Franka/Pico adaptation distribution.
RLinf-Franks remains a source/reference for stable adaptation code, not a second whole-project upstream.
Upstream code may exist without becoming a Release support commitment.
The approved current RLinf baseline remains e7a9a2e until an explicitly verified upstream update is accepted.

verification.summary: Release now has the approved RLinf commit as its grafted base, an explicit RLinf upstream remote, a maintained Franka/Pico adaptation layer, and repeatable no-hardware compatibility checks.
checks: Python compilation for scripts, rig extension, and Pico bridge passed
Shell syntax for supported launchers and adapted RLinf collector passed
RLinf real-world collection and LeRobot writer imports resolved with the Release adaptation paths
limitations: No origin distribution remote is configured because its URL was not provided.
No hardware, Franky/libfranka, vendor Pico SDK, camera, Robotiq, or end-to-end collection run was exercised.
The RLinf ancestry is shallow at the approved baseline until upstream history is fetched.
